newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary meets IMF-agreed 1996 budget target - paper.
newsitem.headline: Hungary meets IMF-agreed 1996 budget target - paper.

text.p: A surge of corporate tax revenues is likely to help Hungary to meet its 1996 general government deficit target agreed with the International Monetary Fund, the daily Napi Gazdasag said on Saturday.
Napi, a usually well-informed paper, referring to unnamed sources said that 1996 corporate tax revenues exceeded the 74 billion forint target by 36 billion forints.

It said the 1996 central state budget deficit, not including one-off revenues and expenditures, amounted to 153 billion forints, down from the 233 billion target, adding that one-off items increased the deficit by 25 billion forints.
The better-than-planned position of the central budget was likely to more or less cover the social security's soaring deficit, Napi said.

The central budget and social security are the main components of the general government budget, the 1996 deficit of which is forecast at four percent of GDP, which is estimated to amount to some 6,600 billion forints in 1996.
The social security deficit had already reached 67.3 billion forints in October, compared to the original 1996 target of 17.8 billion.
Hungary introduced changes in the social security system in 1997 to cut the social security gap to 13 billion forints this year, a target which several analysts called ambitious.

The changes mainly aimed to boost social revenues by forcing former evaders to pay social security contributions and streamlining the costly health care system. --Sandor Peto, Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040
